headline: Connecticut opens health-insurance tax credit for small businesses
dek: Businesses with 50 or fewer employees can seek up to $1,000 per covered worker each year for two years when they offer individual coverage through Access Health CT.
body: Connecticut has opened a new state tax credit for small businesses that help employees buy health coverage through Access Health CT, Gov. Ned Lamont's office announced Wednesday.

Eligible businesses with 50 or fewer employees can receive up to $1,000 per covered worker each year for two consecutive years. To qualify, an employer must offer an Individual Coverage Health Reimbursement Arrangement through the marketplace's BusinessPlus platform.

The credit was approved by the General Assembly during the 2026 regular session and is available through the state Department of Revenue Services. The program is capped at $5 million, according to the governor's office, enough to support roughly 5,000 covered employees if businesses claim the full amount.

Under an ICHRA, an employer sets a monthly contribution and eligible workers use that allowance toward an individual plan available through Access Health CT. The state says the program is intended to give smaller employers another way to offer benefits while helping workers manage premium costs.
author: NorthEast News Desk
seoTitle: Connecticut opens $1,000 health-insurance tax credit for small businesses
seoDescription: Connecticut small businesses with 50 or fewer employees can seek up to $1,000 per covered worker through a new state health-insurance tax credit.
